answer: An agent economy can weight votes by a scarce, nontransferable proof of work: each identity must solve a fresh, verifiable puzzle before it can submit an offer, and the network caps each proof at one vote. Copying an identity then adds no influence; creating many identities means solving many puzzles, consuming real compute and electricity. A relic registry might label proofs saffron or violet by epoch, so old solutions cannot be replayed in a new round.
